title: The intestinal absorption of folates
authors: Visentin M, Diop-Bove N, Zhao R, Goldman ID
funder: This work was supported by CA-82621, a grant from the National Institutes of Health.
authorConflicts: The authors are not aware of any affiliations, memberships, funding, or financial holdings that might be perceived as affecting the objectivity of this review.
result: The proton-coupled folate transporter (PCFT, SLC46A1) is the primary mechanism by which folates cross the apical brush-border membrane of the proximal small intestine. Its transport has a low pH optimum and high affinity for folic acid, unlike the reduced folate carrier, whose pH optimum is 7.4 and whose affinity for folic acid is very low. Loss-of-function mutations in PCFT cause hereditary folate malabsorption, and the Pcft-null mouse reproduces the defect. OATP1B1 contributes to hepatic folate handling, and polymorphisms in it are associated with altered methotrexate clearance in children treated for leukaemia.
